items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: The first first funeral I played right after I got out the name I forgot about was with Peter Bocah and Paul Bob Randall Snare.

ctx.x: You ever played bass drum in the parade?

Yeah. I played lots of bass drums in the funerals. Oh yeah I'm glad you mentioned that. The first first funeral I played right after I got out the name I forgot about was with Peter Bocah and Paul Bob Randall Snare.

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: I know it was led by Peter Boccoff over in Algiers. I played lots of funerals with them on that.

ctx.x: Did they still have some of the old onward band at that time? I didn't know they called it that.

Well, that's what I'm thinking now. I placed several parades and funerals with it, but I know it was led by Peter Boccoff over in Algiers. I played lots of funerals with them on that. I think it was called the Onward Brass Band, part of it. Peter might explain it more better.
Yeah, I don't remember that he told us about that particular group.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: Yeah, he's Daniel Ralphs on Seminoid Street, poor fella, he's the number one wheel writer. He was the leader of that band.

ctx.x: We haven't told Peter Bocard, if we're going to go see him right way.
Yeah, he's Daniel Ralphs on Seminoid Street, poor fella, he's the number one wheel writer. He was the leader of that band.
Oh sure, oh, one of them good ones.
